definitions.explanation: A social group bound by shared ancestry, customs, and territory. Used in anthropological, historical, and geographical contexts.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}には{多|おお}くの{部族|ぶぞく}が{暮|く}らしている。
examples.english: Many tribes live in this region.

examples.japanese: {部族|ぶぞく}{間|かん}の{争|あらそ}いが{続|つづ}いている。
その{部族|ぶぞく}は{独自|どくじ}の{言語|げんご}と{文化|ぶんか}を{守|まも}り{続|つづ}けている。
examples.english: That tribe continues to preserve its own language and culture.

notes:
A compound of {部|ぶ} (section, group) and {族|ぞく} (clan, tribe).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {部族|ぶぞく}{間|かん} (between tribes, intertribal)
- {部族|ぶぞく}{社会|しゃかい} (tribal society)
- {部族|ぶぞく}の{長|おさ} (tribal chief)
- {少数|しょうすう}{部族|ぶぞく} (minority tribe)
- {遊牧|ゆうぼく}{部族|ぶぞく} (nomadic tribe)

Primarily used when discussing indigenous peoples, historical societies, or anthropological topics. In modern Japanese, {民族|みんぞく} (ethnic group, people) is the broader and more common term. {部族|ぶぞく} specifically implies a smaller, more localized group with shared kinship ties.
